The Irish Times — "At least seven reported killed as Russia attacks Ukraine's energy grid". Published Wed 30 September 2026, 16:24 (BST/IST). CONFIRMED 30 Sep, evening-state. (Full text already cached at EVE-WORLD-irishtimes-seven-killed-energy-grid.txt.)

THIS FILE = provenance ledger for the shifting casualty count, because the number moved three times today and the morning edition used the low figure.

WHAT EACH APPROVED SOURCE SUPPORTS:
- 3 killed in Kyiv city, 6 injured (Mayor Vitali Klitschko) — ABC News, 30 Sep 06:15 ET. Cached: EVE-WORLD-abcnews-kyiv-strikes-nato-scramble.txt
- 4 killed including a child, Kyiv + region — AP wire on ABC News, 30 Sep 05:06 ET. Cached: EVE-WORLD-ap-abcnews-kyiv-region-4-killed-power-grid.txt
- 14 injured nationwide (Zelenskyy, morning) — ABC News, same file.
- >>> 7 KILLED nationwide, including a child <<< — The Irish Times, 30 Sep 16:24. THIS IS THE FIGURE THE EVENING EDITION SHOULD CARRY. Irish Times wording: "Ukrainian authorities confirmed seven people were killed in the strikes".
- Air activity: nearly 190 drones plus ballistic missiles; Ukraine's air force downed 5 missiles and 155 drones (Irish Times). ABC News gives the launch figure precisely as 188 drones, 86 of them jet-powered, impacts at 18 locations, and Russia's MoD claiming 384 Ukrainian drones downed.
- Air-raid alert lasted more than 12 hours (Irish Times).
- Critical infrastructure damaged across five regions, further damage in five others (Zelenskyy, via Irish Times). ABC News lists Zhytomyr, Mykolaiv, Kirovohrad, Rivne, Odesa, Sumy, Kharkiv, Kherson and Cherkasy.
- Moldova: a drone crossed into airspace and exploded near the eastern village of Hirbovet. Romania and Poland scrambled jets; Polish airport flights temporarily suspended (Irish Times). ABC News: Romania's defence ministry sent two Spanish F-18s; no airspace incursion.
- Jet-drone escalation data point: 3,177 jet-propelled drones launched through September vs 2,850 in August (Ukrainian Air Force spokesman, via AP on ABC News).

*** NOT SOURCEABLE FROM AN APPROVED OUTLET — DO NOT PRINT ***
"24 injured" nationwide. This is Zelensky's own updated evening figure, given to Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Store. I found it only on Ukrinform (ukrinform.net, 30 Sep 16:54 Kyiv) — a Ukrainian state agency, which is explicitly banned — and on the Los Angeles Times (latimes.com, 30 Sep 14:11 GMT), which is not on the approved list. The AP wire carries it (the LA Times copy is by AP's Hanna Arhirova and Barry Hatton), so an approved AP carrier almost certainly has it: check apnews.com, abcnews.com wireStory and independent.co.uk before publishing. Until then, the highest injury figure I can source from an approved outlet is 14 (ABC News, morning). Floor to print: "at least seven killed, including a child, and at least 14 wounded".
Zelensky's own wording per Ukrinform (BANNED SOURCE — for your hunt only, not for print): "Since the start of the day alone, twenty-four people have been injured. Sadly, seven people have been killed, including a child."
